title: [VSC-4] JetBrains: shared blocker corpus for TaskBlockerPresentation
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). First wave: no dependencies, files disjoint from the other first-wave rows. JetBrains first: this row writes the held-out corpus that VS Code's blocker row (VSC-9) must pass unchanged.

Reuse decision (VSC-0): one client-neutral JSON corpus per shared presentation, executed by both test suites (CQ-I06b pattern, moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-verdicts.json; rule in the header of ClientVerdictCorpusTest.kt: a disagreement is fixed or filed, never given a client-specific expectation). Each new corpus gets its own file.

Objective: block-cause logic exists three times today: JetBrains moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/TaskBlockerPresentation.kt (cause, badges, detail, prerequisiteIds), VS Code moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts (exported blockCause, blockedPrerequisiteIds, blockerFacts) and VS Code moe-vscode/media/board.js (its own blockCause and blockedPrerequisiteIds in browser JS). Pin the client-neutral part as a corpus, with JetBrains as the reference.

Deliverable:
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-blocker.json: `{ "version": 1, "rows": [ { "id": "B01", "task": <task wire JSON>, "cause": "RESOURCE_WAIT" | "DEPENDENCY_WAIT" | "EXTERNAL_BLOCK" | null, "prerequisiteIds": [...], "needsHumanReview": true | false } ] }` (the cause names are the enum both clients already use). At least 14 rows: each cause; a non-BLOCKED status carrying stale block fields (cause null); BLOCKED with blockedOnTaskIds; a reason naming task ids, with and without blockedOnTaskIds (whatever JetBrains derives); duplicate and blank ids; resourceId together with task ids (the precedence JetBrains applies); needsHumanReview true on REVIEW and on BLOCKED, independent of cause; missing optional fields.
- new moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/BlockerCorpusTest.kt: parses each task with MoeJson.parseTask, asserts TaskBlockerPresentation.cause(task)?.name, prerequisiteIds(task) (order included) and the badges' needs-human-review flag against the row, asserts unique `B[0-9]{2}` ids, and reports every failing id at once.
If a row exposes a JetBrains bug, fix TaskBlockerPresentation.kt here and name it in the summary; never bend a row to a bug.

Not in scope: VS Code files (VSC-9), TaskBlockerPresentationTest.kt (unchanged), wording and bundle text (the clients word blocker facts differently on purpose; only the fields above are shared).

Verification (WSL has no JDK): take the `jetbrains-gradle` lease (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease); `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/<dir>`; overlay this task's files; run `cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\<dir>\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun'` (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-snapshot-gradle-test); release the lease even on failure.
definitionOfDone: moe-jetbrains/src/test/resources/client-blocker.json exists with version 1 and at least 14 rows with unique B[0-9]{2} ids, covering every case listed in the description.

BlockerCorpusTest.kt parses each row's task with MoeJson.parseTask and asserts the cause name, prerequisiteIds (order included) and the needs-human-review flag against the row, reporting all failing ids at once.
A scratch-copy mutant that makes TaskBlockerPresentation.cause return a cause for a non-BLOCKED task makes BlockerCorpusTest fail (mutant discarded afterwards).
The full JetBrains suite passes in a git-archive snapshot under the jetbrains-gradle lease: `gradlew.bat test --rerun` reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL, with the JUnit total in the summary.
The diff touches only the two new files, plus TaskBlockerPresentation.kt if a row exposed a JetBrains bug (named in the summary).
